ety.text: Many etymologies have been proposed. The leading theories find its roots in Maghrebi Arabic varieties, primarily from Moroccan Arabic واش (wāš, an interrogative particle), or through ellipsis of Algerian Arabic واش راك (wāš rāk, “what's up?”); in Moroccan Arabic, interrogatives شنو (šnu) and آش (ʔāš) are used to say “what” instead. Certain speakers and online dictionaries like L'internaute propose wesh as a “disformation” of French ouais, though this theory is much less popular.
